questions.stem: A workstation authenticates on a software-switch member, but another member can still reach it without a firewall policy. Which setting is the first design check?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It forces member-to-member frames through firewall policy and session processing.
choices.feedback: Correct: explicit mode makes member traffic policy-controlled instead of automatically bridged.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It enables bridge learning without RADIUS authentication on member ports.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: DHCP and bridge learning do not change the intra-switch policy boundary.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It changes the software switch into a routed aggregate with ECMP.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: explicit intra-switch policy does not convert the interface into a routed aggregate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It makes the switch interface eligible for hardware-only ASIC offload.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the setting controls policy enforcement, not hardware offload eligibility.

questions.stem: A dynamic 802.1X address object remains empty after RADIUS returns Access-Accept. Which response attribute must be checked against the object name?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The NAS-Port-Type value reported for the physical switch port.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: NAS-Port-Type is not the documented group-to-address name mapping.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Fortinet-Group-Name AVP returned by the RADIUS server.
choices.feedback: Correct: the dynamic address-object name must match the Fortinet-Group-Name value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Called-Station-ID string copied from the wireless access point.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: Called-Station-ID is not the address-object mapping contract for this feature.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The DHCP hostname learned after the client obtains an address.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: DHCP hostname is not used to bind the 802.1X dynamic address object.

questions.stem: The 802.1X address dump shows a MAC, interface and VLAN ID. What has this evidence established?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The endpoint's Internet session has matched the intended security policy.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the address table does not prove firewall policy or application-session matching.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The RADIUS server has been installed as the active default gateway.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the dump records authentication binding, not gateway selection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The authenticated endpoint has been bound to the dynamic address object.
choices.feedback: Correct: the entry demonstrates the MAC, interface and VLAN association used by the address object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The software switch has converted every member into a routed interface.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the evidence does not change the interface's Layer-2 switch type.

questions.stem: MAB succeeds and the endpoint reaches the software-switch gateway, but an internal application is denied. What should be checked next?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the RADIUS retransmission count for all access ports.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: successful MAB and gateway reachability move the fault beyond initial authentication.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the DHCP lease duration to match the RADIUS session timeout.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: lease duration does not determine firewall application authorization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable explicit intra-switch policy so the bridge forwards the application automatically.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: that removes the intended policy boundary instead of fixing the denied flow.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Verify the dynamic source object, policy order, destination and service match.
choices.feedback: Correct: authentication and gateway reachability do not prove that the application policy matched.

questions.stem: One FortiSwitch needs a different voice-port setting while the same template remains assigned to twenty other switches. What is the intended 8.0 mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable a device-specific override for that switch and edit only the required port.
choices.feedback: Correct: the override layer records selected deviations for one assigned device.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clone the entire ADOM and move the switch into the duplicate database.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: a new ADOM is unnecessary for a per-device port exception.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the shared template and install it only on the selected switch.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: changing the shared template changes the common baseline for its assignments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove the template and configure every port directly on the switch.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: that discards the centralized baseline and new override workflow.

questions.stem: The Managed FortiSwitches table shows a tooltip icon in the Template column. What should the engineer infer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The switch has failed its last firmware upgrade and is running rollback mode.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the documented icon indicates an override, not firmware state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A device-specific template override has been configured for that switch.
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiManager marks the device when an override has been performed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The template is unassigned and the switch is using factory defaults.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the icon is not an unassigned-template indicator.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every port on the switch is excluded from future template installs.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: an override changes selected settings; it does not exclude every port.

questions.stem: A single port should return to its template value, but the other device-specific exceptions must remain. Which action has the narrowest scope?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable override mode for the entire switch and confirm the warning.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: disabling device override reverts all customized values on that device.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Edit the shared template and replace all port settings with defaults.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: changing the baseline can affect every switch assigned to the template.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Revert All while editing the specific port that should be reset.
choices.feedback: Correct: the documented port-level Revert All discards customizations for that port.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Unassign the template and reassign it after the next maintenance window.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: unassigning and reassigning is broader than the required port-level reset.

questions.stem: A switch still differs from its peers after the override was saved. Which verification best separates stored intent from deployed state?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Check only the shared template name shown in the device list.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the template name alone does not show effective port values or installation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reboot the switch before inspecting any FortiManager configuration.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: a reboot does not establish whether the intended override was installed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable all overrides so every device has an identical configuration.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: that destroys legitimate per-device exceptions without diagnosing the issue.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Compare the override marker, target configuration and install preview for that switch.
choices.feedback: Correct: the marker proves stored deviation; target and install evidence establish deployment intent.

questions.stem: After enabling custom session labels, an administrator logs in but cannot reach the dashboard until a label is entered. Is that expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes; enabling the feature makes a label mandatory for each new login session.
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiAnalyzer prompts for a custom label after successful login and requires it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No; labels are optional metadata and can only be added after logout.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the feature requires a label during the login process.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only administrators with Super_User permission must enter a label.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the feature is enabled globally and makes labels mandatory.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The prompt indicates that the administrator's password was rejected.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the prompt follows successful login and requests session context.

questions.stem: An engineer must prevent a session label from being changed during a maintenance window. Which mode provides that behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Changeable, because it permits an administrator to edit the label at any time.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: changeable mode explicitly allows edits during an active session.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Unique-per-session, because the label cannot change until the session ends.
choices.feedback: Correct: this mode makes the assigned label immutable for that session.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disabled, because no label is stored after the administrator logs in.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: disabled mode turns off the feature rather than fixing a label.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shared-per-admin, because every browser login inherits one administrator label.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the feature supports labels per session, not one permanent label per admin.

questions.stem: Two administrators accidentally use the same change label. What is the correct interpretation of the Event Log?

choices.label: A
choices.text: FortiAnalyzer merges their actions into one authenticated administrator session.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: matching label strings do not merge separate login sessions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The second label is rejected and the second administrator is logged out.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: FortiAnalyzer does not enforce global label uniqueness.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The label is not a globally unique key; correlate it with user and time.
choices.feedback: Correct: uniqueness is not enforced, so other session identifiers remain important.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The duplicate label proves that both administrators used the same browser.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: a repeated label does not establish shared browser or session identity.

questions.stem: A change auditor wants to reconstruct a maintenance session after it ended. Which evidence is the most direct label lookup?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The current FortiAnalyzer firmware image checksum.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the checksum identifies firmware integrity, not an administrator session.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The FortiGate policy package revision and installation timestamp.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: device installation data does not identify every FortiAnalyzer admin action.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Dashboard widget's current CPU and memory graphs.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: resource graphs do not provide session-level action tagging.

choices.label: D
choices.text: System Settings Event Logs filtered by the Custom Session ID column.
choices.feedback: Correct: the Event Log column carries the custom session label for recorded actions.

questions.stem: A two-router RVI transit should not elect a designated router. Which OSPF network type matches that topology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Point-to-point, which suppresses DR and BDR election on that interface.
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiSwitchOS 8.0 documents no DR/BDR election for point-to-point.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Broadcast, which requires a DR and BDR on the segment.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: broadcast Ethernet uses DR/BDR election by default.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Point-to-multipoint, which requires a DR for each neighbor pair.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: point-to-multipoint also avoids DR/BDR election, but the stated topology is a two-router transit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Passive, which removes the interface from the OSPF process.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: passive behavior is not one of the documented network-type choices.

questions.stem: A route cost differs between two routers on the same OSPF domain after one reference-bandwidth change. What is the likely design error?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only the RVI IP address was changed on the FortiSwitch.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: an address change does not explain the reference-bandwidth mismatch.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The routers are using different OSPF reference-bandwidth values.
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet requires the same reference bandwidth on all routers in the OSPF domain.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The DR election timer is shorter on the upstream switch.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: DR election timers do not set the reference-bandwidth cost scale.

choices.label: D
choices.text: IPv6 is enabled on one RVI and IPv4 is enabled on the other.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the feature supports reference bandwidth for both IPv4 and IPv6.

questions.stem: An interface bandwidth is greater than the configured OSPF reference bandwidth. How is the resulting cost treated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It becomes zero so the highest-speed interface always wins.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: OSPF cost is not reduced to zero by this calculation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is copied from the neighbor's most recent LSA.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the local reference-bandwidth formula derives the interface cost.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is set to one when the reference-bandwidth ratio is below one.
choices.feedback: Correct: the documented minimum cost is one when the ratio is below one.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is replaced with the interface's VLAN ID.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: VLAN numbering is unrelated to OSPF cost calculation.

questions.stem: A multi-access Ethernet RVI has several OSPF routers and currently elects a DR. What should be checked before changing it to point-to-point?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whether the FortiAnalyzer report dataset includes the RVI interface name.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: report datasets do not determine OSPF network topology.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whether the FortiManager template has a per-port override marker.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: template overrides are unrelated to OSPF adjacency semantics.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whether all routers have the same administrator password.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: administrator credentials do not determine OSPF network type.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether the segment truly has only two OSPF endpoints and matches point-to-point semantics.
choices.feedback: Correct: suppressing DR election is safe only when the configured type reflects topology.

questions.stem: The FQDN address type is missing when an engineer edits an AP L3 Firewall Profile. What is the first documented prerequisite?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable Advanced Wireless Features under System Feature Visibility.
choices.feedback: Correct: the Fortinet feature procedure requires this visibility option first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable FortiGate Central NAT before editing the AP profile.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: central NAT is not the AP L3 ACL feature prerequisite.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move the SSID into bridge mode and disable the AP profile.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: changing SSID mode does not expose the documented FQDN control.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Install a separate FortiAnalyzer license for the wireless controller.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the FQDN ACL feature is not gated by FortiAnalyzer licensing.

questions.stem: A narrow allow rule for maps.google.com is shadowed by a broad *google.com block. What should the engineer review?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The FortiGate's global DNS database before changing any AP policy.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the immediate policy issue is overlapping AP ACL match scope.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ordering of the specific FQDN rule and the wildcard rule.
choices.feedback: Correct: the specific exception must be evaluated before the broader wildcard match.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The FortiManager ADOM revision number for the wireless profile.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: ADOM revision does not explain local AP ACL rule precedence.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The DHCP lease timer for clients using the affected SSID.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: DHCP timing does not determine which ACL rule matches first.

questions.stem: A wireless client uses IPv6, but the engineer only tested the IPv4 FQDN rule. What is missing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A RADIUS accounting record from the FortiAuthenticator.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: accounting does not establish which address-family ACL matched.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A FortiSwitch port override for the AP uplink.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: a switch template override does not validate the AP IPv6 rule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A test of the IPv6 rule and the actual IPv6 destination path.
choices.feedback: Correct: the feature supports IPv4 and IPv6 rules, so test the family in use.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A FortiPAM secret approval record for the wireless administrator.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: privileged access approvals are unrelated to wireless ACL evaluation.

questions.stem: A hostname's DNS answer changes, but the AP still appears to block the old destination. What is the safest next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assume the ACL immediately refreshes and delete the matching rule.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the indexed feature description does not specify an immediate refresh timer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable every AP L3 Firewall Profile and rely only on upstream routing.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: that removes the intended enforcement point without isolating the cause.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the FortiGate address object to the new IP and ignore the AP profile.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: changing a FortiGate object does not update the AP L3 ACL rule.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Verify the AP profile, current name resolution and observed allow/block behavior after convergence.
choices.feedback: Correct: validate the effective AP policy and DNS state without assuming a refresh interval.

questions.stem: A branch wants FortiNAC itself to process MAC authentication and 802.1X EAP rather than forward requests to an external server. Which mode fits?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable the built-in Local RADIUS authentication mode.
choices.feedback: Correct: Local RADIUS can process MAC and EAP authentication within FortiNAC.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use only the external RADIUS proxy mode for every request.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: proxy mode forwards authentication to another RADIUS server.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable RADIUS and use DHCP fingerprinting as the authentication method.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: DHCP fingerprinting is not a RADIUS authentication mode.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Send all EAP requests to FortiAnalyzer before policy evaluation.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: FortiAnalyzer is not the Local RADIUS authentication engine.

questions.stem: Local RADIUS returns Access-Accept, but the accounting server receives no session records. Which explanation is documented?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Local RADIUS automatically writes accounting to the FortiNAC event database only.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the guide states Local RADIUS does not provide accounting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Local RADIUS does not provide accounting; proxy accounting externally if required.
choices.feedback: Correct: authentication and accounting are separate, and accounting can be proxied externally.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The endpoint's EAP method is unsupported because Access-Accept was returned.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: a successful Access-Accept does not explain the missing accounting path.

choices.label: D
choices.text: FortiNAC must be converted to a RADIUS client before accounting can work.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the documented design can proxy accounting without changing the local authentication role.

questions.stem: Both Local RADIUS and Proxy RADIUS modes are enabled, and requests intermittently hit the wrong service. What configuration conflict should be checked?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The shared FortiGate software-switch interface name.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: interface naming does not resolve FortiNAC RADIUS listener collisions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The LDAP group name returned by FortiAuthenticator.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: group naming is unrelated to local/proxy listener port allocation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The authentication port numbers assigned to Local and Proxy RADIUS.
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet warns that authentication ports must differ when both modes are configured.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer report hcache retention interval.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: report caching does not affect RADIUS listener ports.

questions.stem: Which EAP method is explicitly listed as supported by the FortiNAC Local RADIUS server?

choices.label: A
choices.text: EAP-FAST with PAC provisioning only.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: EAP-FAST is not in the documented Local RADIUS method list.

choices.label: B
choices.text: EAP-SIM with carrier-derived subscriber credentials.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: EAP-SIM is not listed for the Local RADIUS feature.

choices.label: C
choices.text: EAP-PWD with a password-authenticated key exchange.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: EAP-PWD is not listed in the guide's supported set.

choices.label: D
choices.text: PEAP with MSCHAPv2 inner authentication.
choices.feedback: Correct: PEAP/MSCHAPv2 is one of the four documented methods.

questions.stem: A legacy deployment has a Manager plus separate Control and Application servers. Which migration guide should be selected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The FortiNAC-OS migration guide for Manager environments with separate C+A servers.
choices.feedback: Correct: the procedure must match both Manager management and separate C+A topology.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The single-appliance CA migration guide because it has fewer cutover steps.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: a single-appliance guide does not describe separate C+A roles.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The FortiPAM cross-platform restore article because both products use appliance backups.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: FortiPAM backup guidance is unrelated to FortiNAC migration topology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The N+1 failover guide even if no N+1 group is configured.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: N+1 failover is not the same as a CentOS-to-NAC-OS migration.

questions.stem: The source FortiNAC uses subscription endpoint licenses. What should the migration plan assume?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Customer Service will always transfer every subscription entitlement to the new serial.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the guide distinguishes perpetual from subscription support types.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A new endpoint license is required because subscription entitlements are not transferred.
choices.feedback: Correct: subscription or combined entitlements require a new endpoint license.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The configuration backup itself carries the entitlement to any new appliance.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: a configuration file does not transfer the licensing contract.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The target must retain the old serial number after the cutover.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the new appliance has its own serial and registration process.

questions.stem: The migration is complete and the new appliance has inherited the old IP addresses. When should a planned IP change occur?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Before collecting migration data so the new server starts on the final address.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the guide says IP changes should be made after migration completes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the version check while the migration tool is running.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: changing addressing during cutover risks breaking the migration transaction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: After the migration is complete and the new appliance is operational.
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet explicitly places any required IP change after migration.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only after deleting the old appliance from FortiNAC Manager.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the documented sequence does not require deleting the old appliance first.

questions.stem: After migration, SNMP traps are no longer received from a managed switch. What is the first FortiNAC-OS-specific check?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the SNMP polling interval on every managed switch.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: polling interval does not open the FortiNAC interface service.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Restore the old CentOS firewall rules without reviewing the new OS.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the migration guide highlights FortiNAC-OS's restricted default port exposure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable the endpoint license check and reboot the CA server.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: licensing is not the direct reason SNMP traffic is discarded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Verify SNMP is included in the appropriate interface allowaccess list.
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiNAC-OS discards traffic for services not enabled on the interface.

questions.stem: A Windows account ends in $, but the administrator does not want to discard every such string blindly. What does FortiAuthenticator 6.6.7 do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It checks AD to classify the account as computer or user.
choices.feedback: Correct: the feature classifies the object through AD before excluding computer accounts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It drops every username containing a dollar sign without querying the directory.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the documented mechanism is an AD lookup, not suffix-only filtering.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It converts the account into a local FortiAuthenticator user group.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the feature excludes computer accounts from FSSO rather than creating a group.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It asks FortiGate to classify the account after the FSSO update.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: classification occurs on FortiAuthenticator before FSSO propagation.

questions.stem: A computer account is still visible as an FSSO user after enabling the new option. Which check is most relevant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The FortiGate SD-WAN policy's preferred underlay bandwidth mode.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: SD-WAN steering is unrelated to FSSO account classification.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whether the active FSSO method has filtering enabled and can query AD.
choices.feedback: Correct: the filter depends on the active method and an AD object lookup.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer session-label mode for administrator logins.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: admin session labels do not change Windows account classification.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The RADIUS accounting proxy's NAS-IP rewrite setting.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: RADIUS accounting transformation is unrelated to FSSO filtering.

questions.stem: A valid human account is not propagated after the computer-account filter is enabled. What is the best test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rename the user so the username no longer contains punctuation.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: changing identity names is not a safe diagnostic for directory classification.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable all FSSO methods and rebuild the FortiGate user database.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: this destroys useful state and does not isolate the AD lookup.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Compare known user and computer objects through the same AD lookup.
choices.feedback: Correct: paired test objects show whether classification or the FSSO method is failing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a duplicate local user on FortiAuthenticator with the same username.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: a local duplicate does not validate the AD object lookup.

questions.stem: A suffix-based filter is proposed as a substitute for the 6.6.7 feature. What is the key weakness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It requires every workstation to use the same IP address.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: IP addressing is not the key classification issue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It changes RADIUS accounting records but leaves FSSO unchanged.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the proposed filter is about FSSO identity handling.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It forces computer accounts to authenticate using PEAP-MAB.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: PEAP-MAB is not part of this feature's account classification.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A string suffix cannot reliably distinguish a computer object from a user object.
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiAuthenticator uses AD lookup because the suffix alone is insufficient.

questions.stem: A FortiPAM backup restores system settings and secrets, but old session videos and secret logs are missing. What is the expected explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: System Events, secret logs and videos are not included in the configuration backup file.
choices.feedback: Correct: those records are separate from the configuration backup payload.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The backup was encrypted with the wrong password so videos were skipped.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: encryption protects the backup file; videos are not included in that file.

choices.label: C
choices.text: FortiPAM only backs up video files when the appliance is in Stop mode.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: remote video storage is separate and requires Rolling mode.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The restore process automatically deletes all secret activity from FortiAnalyzer.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the backup content boundary does not imply deletion of external logs.

questions.stem: A restore is planned while private-data-encryption is enabled. What must be done before restoring the backup?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable all secret launchers and remove the FortiPAM license.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: those actions do not supply the key needed to decrypt private data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable private-data-encryption with the same 32-hexadecimal key first.
choices.feedback: Correct: the documented restore example requires the same key before restore.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Export all session videos into the configuration backup file.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: videos are not included in the configuration backup payload.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change every target password manually before uploading the backup.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: credential rotation is not the encryption-key precondition.

questions.stem: A backup may contain a password that is no longer current because a password changer ran after the backup. What is Fortinet's recommended control?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the SFTP server's file retention and restore the newest filename only.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: retention does not prevent a concurrent password change during backup.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable the password changer permanently across all secrets.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the guide recommends a controlled maintenance-mode backup, not permanent disablement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enter maintenance mode so no password changer runs, then trigger the backup.
choices.feedback: Correct: maintenance mode protects the backup from a concurrent password-rotation transaction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Export only the system event log and use it as the credential database.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: event logs do not contain the current secret values.

questions.stem: A team assumes that restoring a FortiPAM configuration backup is an officially supported cross-platform migration. Which statement is safest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any FortiPAM backup can be restored to FortiSRA if the IP address is unchanged.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: product type and platform compatibility are not interchangeable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: FortiConverter automatically translates all FortiPAM appliance platform identifiers during restore.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the recent Community article says FortiConverter does not support this migration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The configuration file includes all videos and audit logs needed for a full clone.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: logs and videos are not contained in the configuration backup.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Backup/restore is documented, but cross-platform migration is not an official supported procedure.
choices.feedback: Correct: keep the recovery workflow distinct from the unsupported platform-migration scenario.

questions.stem: After a Windows Agent upgrade, raw events arrive as XML but custom fields disappear. What is the most likely parser-side cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A custom parser still expects the previous flat attribute/value format.
choices.feedback: Correct: the agent now sends native XML and custom parsers must be updated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Windows agent is sending only UDP accounting packets to FortiNAC.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the described issue is a parser-schema mismatch, not RADIUS accounting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer report hcache has expired before the Collector reads the event.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: hcache is not the Windows event parser.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The FortiGate software switch has assigned the endpoint to the wrong VLAN.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: VLAN assignment does not explain missing XML-parsed fields.

questions.stem: A team plans to upgrade thousands of Windows Agents. What must happen before the rollout?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delete all custom Windows parsers so the Collector accepts any event format.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: deleting parsers removes required normalization and detection logic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Update and test custom parsers against native XML before upgrading agents.
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet explicitly requires custom parsers to be upgraded before the agent change.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Upgrade the Agents first, then compare a sample of raw messages afterward.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: that sequence risks a large-scale parsing gap.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Move all Windows Event Logs into FortiAnalyzer before upgrading the Collector.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: this does not resolve the FortiSIEM parser schema transition.

questions.stem: A 7.1.x deployment has empty Message nodes and incomplete Windows Agent XML events. Which content update is called out by Fortinet?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Content Update 450, which changes FortiGate traffic-log field names.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: that content update is not the documented Windows Agent parser fix.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A FortiNAC endpoint fingerprint package for Windows devices.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: endpoint profiling packages do not update FortiSIEM XML parsing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Content Update 606 for FortiSIEM 7.1.x.
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet identifies Content Update 606 for the WinOSXmlParser improvement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A FortiManager ADOM metadata variable update to 32,768 characters.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: FortiManager metadata variables are unrelated to Windows event parsing.

questions.stem: Why can endpoint CPU decrease while Collector CPU rises slightly after the native XML transfer change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Agent encrypts every Windows event twice before sending it.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the change is not described as duplicate encryption.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Collector stops receiving Forwarded Events and processes fewer records.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: Forwarded Events are included in the native XML transfer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Windows Agent compresses all event logs into a FortiGate VPN tunnel.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the documented change concerns where parsing occurs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Parsing moves from the Windows Agent to the Collector's WinOSXmlParser.
choices.feedback: Correct: the work is shifted from endpoint parsing to Collector parsing.

questions.stem: A user exceeds a configured FortiSASE bandwidth limit. What is the documented enforcement behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Policing drops traffic that exceeds the configured bandwidth limit.
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiSASE describes bandwidth control as policing, not queuing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The excess traffic is always buffered until the profile becomes available.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the feature description says excess traffic is dropped.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The user's IPsec tunnel is automatically terminated after one over-limit packet.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: policing does not imply tunnel teardown.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The FortiGate WAN interface is rate-limited before traffic reaches the PoP.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: FortiSASE applies the policy to matching IPsec agent-tunnel traffic.

questions.stem: A shared profile must limit traffic in the destination-to-source direction. Which policy option should be enabled?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Per-IP profile, because it only shapes the source-to-destination direction.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: per-IP profiles apply in both directions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reverse direction of shared profile, because shared profiles are directional.
choices.feedback: Correct: the reverse-direction option applies the shared profile destination-to-source.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implicit Medium Control, because it reverses every policy automatically.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the implicit policy is predefined and does not reverse a chosen shared profile.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Application Override, because it changes the traffic direction before policing.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: application overrides are unrelated to bandwidth direction.

questions.stem: A broad bandwidth policy matches before a specific voice policy. Why might voice traffic receive the wrong profile?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Shared profiles are evaluated after every per-IP profile regardless of policy order.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the documented matching sequence is top-down.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The IPsec tunnel ignores user and service matching when bandwidth is enabled.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: user, service and other fields are policy match criteria.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bandwidth-control policies are matched top-down, so the broad rule may win first.
choices.feedback: Correct: more granular rules should be placed above general policies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The FortiSASE PoP chooses the profile using the endpoint MAC address only.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the feature matches configured IP/header and upper-layer criteria.

questions.stem: A bandwidth policy matches an application name, but traffic never hits the expected rule. What prerequisite should be checked?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A FortiAnalyzer custom session label for the user's browser login.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: administrator session labels do not classify application traffic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A FortiSwitch OSPF network type for the user's access VLAN.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: OSPF network type does not identify application traffic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A FortiNAC local RADIUS accounting proxy for the endpoint.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: RADIUS accounting is not the application-control prerequisite.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An Application Control profile in a policy that identifies the selected application.
choices.feedback: Correct: the guide requires Application Control for application-based bandwidth matching.

questions.stem: Four IPsec overlays share two physical WAN ports. The design must compare physical circuit capacity, not each tunnel independently. Which setting applies?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set bandwidth-type underlay on the load-balance service.
choices.feedback: Correct: underlay mode evaluates the shared physical WAN capacity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep bandwidth-type overlay so every tunnel is measured independently.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: overlay is the default and measures individual overlay availability.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable load-balance and create one static route per spoke.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the feature is designed for load-balance services.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set every member to round-robin and ignore bandwidth estimates.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: round-robin does not select by shared underlay availability.

questions.stem: An application is sensitive to both incoming and outgoing capacity. Which hash mode considers both directions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: inbandwidth, because it selects the member with the best outgoing capacity.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: inbandwidth considers incoming available bandwidth.

choices.label: B
choices.text: bibandwidth, because it considers incoming and outgoing available bandwidth.
choices.feedback: Correct: bidirectional bandwidth mode evaluates both directions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: outbandwidth, because it uses the sum of both directional values.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: outbandwidth considers outgoing capacity only.

choices.label: D
choices.text: round-robin, because it uses the current utilization of both directions.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: round-robin does not use the documented bandwidth hash selection.

questions.stem: The service output lists members as alive and shows different bibandwidth values. What does that output establish?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The application has achieved the expected end-to-end throughput.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: member selection evidence does not measure application throughput.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ISP has committed to the displayed bandwidth for the next hour.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: the diagnostic output is a current selection snapshot, not an ISP guarantee.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Which eligible members and bandwidth values the service used for selection.
choices.feedback: Correct: the output exposes service mode, member health and calculated bandwidth values.

choices.label: D
choices.text: That every overlay has an independent physical WAN circuit.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: several overlays can share one underlay circuit.

questions.stem: A bandwidth estimate is high, but traffic still avoids the overlay. Which pair of conditions should be checked together?

choices.label: A
choices.text: FortiAnalyzer report caching and FortiManager administrator session labels.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: neither affects SD-WAN member eligibility or bandwidth selection.

choices.label: B
choices.text: FortiNAC registration status and FortiAuthenticator computer-account filtering.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: endpoint identity feeds do not determine the SD-WAN service member.

choices.label: C
choices.text: FortiAP FQDN ACL order and FortiSwitch private VLAN membership.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: wireless ACL and Layer-2 isolation do not establish SD-WAN selection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The member's SLA eligibility and the service's load-balance/hash/bandwidth-type settings.
choices.feedback: Correct: a high bandwidth value cannot make a failed or ineligible member usable.

questions.stem: A feature test succeeds in a control-plane table, but the application still fails. Which troubleshooting discipline is most reliable?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Treat each evidence surface as proof of its stage, then verify the next.
choices.feedback: Correct: authentication, object binding, route selection and application sessions are separate proofs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume the first successful control-plane status proves the full data path.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: one stage's success does not prove downstream policy or forwarding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change every related product configuration at once to remove uncertainty.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: simultaneous changes destroy fault isolation and causal evidence.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a dashboard screenshot as the sole acceptance test for the feature.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: a dashboard view rarely proves the complete packet or identity transaction.

questions.stem: A candidate topic has a new article URL but its mechanism matches a lesson from last week. What should happen before generation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accept it because the URL and publication date are different.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: URL novelty does not establish semantic novelty.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reject it if the feature/workflow/evidence/remediation fingerprint is substantially equivalent.
choices.feedback: Correct: the rolling exclusion is semantic, not a title or URL comparison.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rename the lesson and keep the same packet or identity mechanism.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: renaming does not change the underlying lesson mechanism.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Publish it as a scenario even when the article is the only primary source.
choices.feedback: Incorrect: Community troubleshooting material is scenario evidence, not a substitute for an authoritative primary lesson.
